title: Never let money be emitted or persisted as a JSON number
summary: Rexx strings have numeric semantics and json.cls may emit a numeric-looking Rexx string as a JSON number. Money and opaque identifiers are therefore always encoded with a protection prefix on the persisted wire, and money is reconstructed through the same 50-digit validator on recovery.
evidence_note: PERSISTENCE_AND_PRECISION_CONTRACT v0.6: because json.cls can coerce numeric-looking Rexx strings, all persisted data scalars carry a storage protection prefix. Physical JSONL represents an amount as the string "S:I:<digits>"; the S: layer also preserves opaque leading-zero identifiers and evidence references such as 00123456 and 000123.
invariants: A monetary amount is represented as an I:-prefixed canonical minor-unit string, never as a bare JSON number.

Persisted scalars carry an S: storage layer so opaque identifiers and evidence references survive a JSON round-trip; on recovery S: is removed, I: is validated, and the digits pass through the 50-digit whole-minor-unit validator.
Do not let a persistence or transport boundary convert a large numeric string into a JSON number and back.
One durable store holds one accounting book for one legal entity; a store does not create cross-company authority.
